newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, Russia reach direct flight accord.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, Russia reach direct flight accord.

text.p: Taiwan said on Friday it had reached agreement on direct air links with Russia that would allow flights to begin in two months, but did not include extension of flights beyond Taipei and Moscow.
A Foreign Ministry official said the agreement would include two weekly round-trip flights each by Taiwan's China Airlines and Russia's TransAero.

"Our government is very pleased with the major achievement of realising direct flights (between Taipei and Moscow)," the state-run Central News Agency quoted James Wang, director of the ministry's West Asian Affairs department, as saying.
"Direct flights will be able to begin in two months," Wang said.
Wang said the two sides failed to discuss flight extensions during negotiations held in Moscow from March 5-6, which China Airlines had said would help business.
But he said further talks would be held later this year.

Taipei and Moscow had agreed in principle in 1993 to forge air links, but direct flights have been stalled by doubts over profitability and protests from China, which views Taiwan as a renegade province ineligible for international ties.
Nevertheless, Taiwan has direct air links with many nations, including the United States.
In February, China expressed anger at a secret aviation pact between Cambodia and Taiwan, which plans to commence flights from Taipei to Phnom Penh at the end of March.
China and Taiwan have been divided since the nationalists fled to the island in 1949 after losing their civil war to the communists on the mainland.
